title: Eliminate latency spiral from ingress phase-shift in continuous batcher
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (two enterprise Dedicated customers and one Hosted customer support ticket) reported sudden increases in p95/p99 token latency that correlated with maintenance waves and autoscaler oscillations. Problem only reproduces under mixed-length workloads with a small-but-steady stream of short requests and intermittent long-context requests. The continuous batcher enters a recurring phase-shift: short-request velocity collapses repeatedly while long-context inflight windows monopolize admission, producing a latency spiral and queue starvation for low-latency flows.

Background: We previously observed related long-tail failures but those fixes (admission smoothing and prefetch quarantine) reduced incidence; this regression is triggered by a timing/race between ingress admission updates and the batcher tick alignment after host maintenance or node scaling events. Customers saw production degradations during scheduled maintenance windows and during sudden autoscaler bursts.

Why this ticket: This issue produced a P0 support escalation (customer-impacting SLO misses) and requires an operational fix + robust upstream change to the admission/tick interaction in the continuous batcher runtime. The goal is to ship a targeted patch to stop the spiral within 72 hours and follow with a more defensive redesign for the next release.
observed_symptoms:
- p95 token latency increased 2–4x for short requests for 8–30 minutes after maintenance or scaling events.
- Short requests queue depth grows while KV cache churn spikes.
- Telemetry shows repeated large batches formed by long-context requests interleaving with microbursts of short flows that never get admitted.
- Host-level event timeline aligns: k8s cordon/drain -> node rejoin -> batcher tick slip -> admission window drift.
- Customers: Hosted customer #8421 dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/customers/8421/incidents/2026-01-26
root_cause: Race between the admission window recalculation (triggered by ingress + autoscaler events) and the batcher tick scheduler. When ticks slip, the inflight reservation accounting for long-context batches is not reconciled atomically with the admission reservoir, allowing long-context inflight to claim admission repeatedly while short requests see their reservation decremented but not replenished. The result is an emergent starvation loop amplified by our current backoff logic which scales admission down instead of rebalancing across length classes.
reproduction_steps:
1) Deploy a mixed-load generator: 200 qps of short requests (<=64 tokens, mean latency target 20ms) plus 2 qps of long-context requests (>=4096 tokens).
2) Schedule a rolling node drain (simulate maintenance) on the host pool.
3) Observe post-drain for 5–20 minutes: p95 of short flow spikes while long flows remain serviced.
4) Collect runtime traces with batcher debug logging (enable BATCHER_TRACE=1) and dump admission reservoirs.
Notes: reproduces reliably in dedicated staging with same config and in a tight simulated hosted environment when admission is enabled.
mitigation:
- Hotfix (deployed 2026-02-02): make admission reservoir reconciliation idempotent on tick re-sync. This prevents double-claiming of inflight slots by long-context batches during a tick slip.
- Short-term config: enable conservative ingress gating for mixed-length traffic (config flag runtime.ingress.conservative_mixed_mode=true) for affected customers until full rollout.
- Customer support actions: notify affected tenants, enable conservative gating, revert non-essential autoscaler rules if on Dedicated.
fix_notes:
Code changes (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4267):
- Add a reconciliation step in BatchTick::onResync() to re-evaluate and refill short-request reservation buckets atomically with inflight accounting.
- Replace a non-atomic decrement+schedule path with an atomic reservation delta and backoff window reset.
- Add unit tests simulating tick slip and mixed-length admission mix.
- Add a defensive metric: admission_reconcile_mismatches (counter) and reconcile_duration_ms (histogram).
rollout_plan:
1) Canary build to 3 hosts in staging, run mixed-load test for 4 hours.
2) Canary in Hosted canaries (5% traffic) with slow ramp and tight alerting on p95 and admission_reconcile_mismatches.
3) If stable for 24 hours, rollout to Dedicated pools with customer opt-in and scheduled maintenance windows.
4) Post-rollout: keep conservative gating enabled for 72 hours for high-risk tenants.
Rollback: revert PR and switch conservative_mixed_mode to true if anomalies detected.
telemetry_queries:
- p95_short_requests: query token_latencies{request_length_bucket="short"} by deployment and host.
- admission_mismatch_count: sum(admission_reconcile_mismatches) by host over 1m.
- kv_cache_evictions: rate(kv_cache_evictions[5m]) correlated with long-context inflight count.
- quick dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/boards/cont-batcher/ingress-phase-shift
postmortem_action_items:
- (Owner: Brendan) Harden admission reconciliation code paths and add formal model proofs for atomicity in the tick transition (due 2026-03-05).
- (Owner: Mei Chen) Expand chaos tests (node drain + mixed load) in CI with admission invariants validated (due 2026-02-28).
- (Owner: Support Ops) Update runbook to include quick toggle for conservative_mixed_mode and checklist for scheduled maintenance (due 2026-02-10).
- (Owner: DX) Add an alert that surfaces admission_reconcile_mismatches >= 10 in 5m window (due 2026-02-04).
customer_notes:
- 2026-01-27: Hosted customer #8421 reported sustained tail latency after our scheduled region maintenance. Assigned to oncall, immediate mitigation applied (conservative gating).
- 2026-01-29: Dedicated customer 'FinApp' escalated revenue-impacting delays during end-of-day processing; we applied hotfix and scheduled dedicated maintenance window.
- Support PR: https://go.redwood.example/support/INC-9928
